qs.q: A middle-aged man cannot taste anything on the posterior portion of his tongue during a cranial nerve examination. Which specific nerve provides sensory innervation to this anatomical area?
o: The hypoglossal nerve via intrinsic branches
The facial nerve via the chorda tympani
The trigeminal nerve via the lingual branch
The vagus nerve via superior laryngeal branch
qs.e: Taste sensation for the posterior one-third of the tongue is supplied exclusively by the glossopharyngeal nerve.

qs.q: During a routine cranial nerve examination, a patient is asked to clench their teeth while the examiner palpates the masseter muscles. Which nerve is being tested?
o: Lingual division of the hypoglossal nerve
Temporal motor branch of the facial nerve
Mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve
Motor component of the glossopharyngeal nerve
Sternocleidomastoid branch of the accessory nerve
qs.e: The mandibular division of CN V innervates the muscles of mastication like the masseter.
